reason: The text portrays the primary elite figure, Joseph (who serves as governor of Egypt), very favorably. He demonstrates wisdom, restraint, compassion, and eventually mercy toward his brothers. Pharaoh is also depicted as reasonable and generous, granting Joseph's family the best land and provisions. While the narrative includes Joseph testing his brothers and showing his authority, this serves the redemptive arc of the story rather than critiquing the elite class. The Egyptian officials and servants who appear are portrayed neutrally. The unfavorable portrayals in the text concern Joseph's brothers' past sin of selling him into slavery, not members of the elite establishment.
